name: Spanish Governor's Palace
aka: Comandancia of the Presidio San Antonio de Béxar

location.text: 105 Plaza de Armas, San Antonio, Texas

dates.note: The Wikipedia infobox prints 'Built 1749'; the city's archaeology report says 'circa 1749 based on the date carved in the keystone found above the main entrance'. Restored 1930-31 (the report quotes the restoration architect, Smith, in 1931). The Library's HABS record is measured drawings and field records; its data PDF carries no date.
dates.altered: Restored 1930-31; the restoration architect located stone footings behind the building and added rooms at the rear on them (the city's archaeology report, quoting Smith, 1931).

refs.title: Spanish Governor's Palace, 105 Plaza de Armas, San Antonio, Bexar County, TX
refs.note: The search result's own line: 'Call Number: HABS TX-3540'. The data PDF at tile.loc.gov/.../tx/tx1000/tx1093/data/tx1093data.pdf was read twice on 4 Sep 2026 and returned only its cover each time: 'SPANISH GOVERNOR'S PALACE HABS TX-3540 105 Plaza de Armas TX-3540 San Antonio Bexar Texas REDUCED COPIES OF MEASURED DRAWINGS FIELD RECORDS HISTORIC AMERICAN BUILDINGS SURVEY ...'. A drawings-and-field-records record with no written description, so no `survey` block is recorded.

refs.title: NRHP reference No. 70000741; added April 15, 1970; designated NHL April 15, 1970 (as the Wikipedia infobox prints it)
Spanish Governor's Palace (U.S. National Park Service)
refs.note: 'The complex includes a one-story masonry and stucco structure with ten rooms, a well-manicured courtyard, and a fountain'; 'Also known as the Comandancia, or command headquarters, the building was part of the presidio'; 'Only one acting governor ever lived there'.

refs.title: Restoration and Previous Archaeology At the Spanish Governor's Palace, San Antonio, Bexar County, Texas (Kristi M. Ulrich, Center for Archaeological Research, UTSA)
refs.note: 'The structure is believed to have been constructed circa 1749 based on the date carved in the keystone found above the main entrance'; quotes the 1931 restoration architect (Smith) on locating stone footings of the rooms 'we added in the rear'.

refs.title: History & Culture (Spanish Governor's Palace, City of San Antonio World Heritage Office)
refs.note: Owner. Adina De Zavala in 1915 'called it the Spanish Governor's Palace, even though it had actually been the home and office of the local presidio' commander.

note: Added 4 Sep 2026 as the Texas province's domestic-scale building in stone, for a node whose regions list Texas and whose exemplars named none. The loc.gov search also surfaced HABS TX-222 (San Antonio City Hall), whose record mentions the 'Old Spanish Governor's Palace' in passing; not opened.
